info.title: Api
info.description:
Sun and Moon positions, day events, crossings and alignments from JPL DE440. Every response carries provenance (implementation, ephemeris, DE440 blocks read, compute time, cache tiers) and, for /v1/position, /v1/day, /v1/crossing and /v1/alignment, a conventions block with every threshold, horizon, refraction input and geoid value used.

Changes on 2026-10-29 (API correctness pass):
1. /v1/day rise and set now depend on height. An explicit `height` is metres above the WGS-84 ellipsoid (unchanged meaning), and the sea-horizon dip is taken from the height above mean sea level (EGM96). Example: in New York `height=0` is ≈ 33 m above sea level, so sunrise is ≈ 1 min earlier and sunset ≈ 1 min later than before. Pass `heightRef=msl` for a height above sea level (iOS `altitude`, maps); omit `height` to stand at sea level, which gives the previous times (Sun within 1 ms).
2. `apparentAltitude` in /v1/position is now `number | null`: refraction is applied down to the observer's horizon (default the sea horizon, −dip) and the value is null below it or below −1.6963°. It used to repeat the true altitude below −1°. One refraction model now serves every endpoint (34′ at the horizon), so apparent altitudes are 1.3 % of the refraction lower than Skyfield's Bennett (0.45′ at 0°, 0.07′ at 10°), and /v1/crossing at apparent 0° (upper limb) equals /v1/day's sunrise.
3. Unknown query parameters are rejected with 400 InvalidRequest (kind UnknownParameter, with the allowed list). They used to be ignored.
4. New: /v1/crossing; on /v1/day `temperature`, `pressure`, `horizon` (sea | geometric | degrees), `horizonProfile`, `limb`; `heightRef` everywhere; `altitudeRate` and `azimuthRate` (°/min) in positions; observer heightMsl and geoidUndulation.
5. New (2026-10-29): /v1/track, the sampled Sun and Moon azimuth / altitude / apparent altitude over a UTC grid in one immutable answer (what the homepage draws its paths from).

Changes on 2026-10-30 (round-2 feedback):
6. /v1/alignment: `heightRef` (observer) and `targetHeightRef`, each ellipsoid (default) | msl, as on /v1/crossing; `target` echoes the target's heights and geoid undulation; every track point has `altitudeRate`, `azimuthRate` (°/min, as /v1/position), `heightEllipsoid`, `heightMsl`, `geoidUndulation`; a `conventions` block. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: without `observerHeight` the eye is now on the geoid (heightMsl 0, as on every other endpoint); it used to be 0 m above the ellipsoid (≈ 33 m below sea level in New York).
7. `include=sun,phase` on /v1/alignment (per track point and pass) and /v1/crossing (per crossing): the Sun's azimuth, true and apparent altitude seen from that point, and the Moon's phase.

height.description: Metres above the WGS-84 ellipsoid (same as heightEllipsoid; kept for compatibility).

heightMsl.description: Metres above the EGM96 geoid (≈ mean sea level).

geoidUndulation.description: EGM96 N, metres: heightEllipsoid = heightMsl + geoidUndulation.

heightRef.description: What the request's height was measured from; default = no height given, the observer is on the geoid.

apparentAltitude.description: Refracted altitude, degrees; null when it would lie below the observer's horizon or the refraction model's floor (conventions.refraction.validFrom). CHANGED 2026-10-29: was always a number, and repeated the true altitude below −1°.

altitudeRate.description: d(altitude)/dt, degrees per minute (true altitude; symmetric difference over ±10 s).

azimuthRate.description: d(azimuth)/dt, degrees per minute (symmetric difference over ±10 s).

apparentAltitude.description: Refracted altitude, degrees; null when it would lie below the observer's horizon or the refraction model's floor (conventions.refraction.validFrom). CHANGED 2026-10-29: was always a number, and repeated the true altitude below −1°.

altitudeRate.description: d(altitude)/dt, degrees per minute (true altitude; symmetric difference over ±10 s).

azimuthRate.description: d(azimuth)/dt, degrees per minute (symmetric difference over ±10 s).

validFrom.description: Lowest apparent altitude that gets a value: max(horizon, the model floor −1.6963°). Below it apparentAltitude is null.

altitude.description: Apparent altitude of the horizon, degrees (null for a profile).

dip.description: Sea-horizon dip, degrees: √(1 − k)·acos(R/(R + heightMsl)), k = terrestrialRefractionK, R = 6 371 008.8 m.

count.description: Samples: sample i is at start + i·stepSeconds; (end − start)/stepSeconds + 1.

azimuth.description: Degrees from north through east, [0, 360), one per sample.

apparentAltitude.description: Refracted altitude, degrees; null below the observer's horizon or the refraction model's floor, exactly as /v1/position.

validFrom.description: Lowest apparent altitude that gets a value: max(horizon, the model floor −1.6963°). Below it apparentAltitude is null.

altitude.description: Apparent altitude of the horizon, degrees (null for a profile).

dip.description: Sea-horizon dip, degrees: √(1 − k)·acos(R/(R + heightMsl)), k = terrestrialRefractionK, R = 6 371 008.8 m.

declination.description: Magnetic declination, degrees, east positive. Magnetic bearing = true bearing − declination.

inValidityWindow.description: WMM2025 is valid 2025.0–2030.0; outside it the secular variation is extrapolated.

magneticDeclination.description: WMM2025 at the observer, height 0, now; east positive. Full precision (was rounded to 0.01° before 2026-10-29): the same value /v1/magnetic gives for lat/lon now.

observationStale.description: Observation older than 75 minutes (METARs are hourly).

distanceKm.description: Great-circle distance from the observer (sphere of radius 6 371.0088 km).

true.description: Initial great-circle bearing from the observer to the station, degrees true, [0, 360).

magnetic.description: The same bearing, degrees magnetic (true − WMM2025 declination at the observer).

directionDegTrue.description: Direction the wind blows from, degrees true; null when calm or variable.

orMore.description: Reported as N+ (e.g. 10+): at least N.

fetchedAt.description: When this Worker last confirmed the feed with aviationweather.gov (200 or 304).

stale.description: Older than the 60 s fresh window (served while a refresh runs, or because upstream failed).

tier.description: Workers Caching status of the feed fetch, lower-cased cf-cache-status (hit, updating = served stale while it refreshes, miss/expired = fetched from aviationweather.gov, revalidated = 304 from upstream); stale-on-error = the feed fetch failed and this isolate's last copy answered; none = no cache (dev).
